title: Editorial & Review Functions
kicker: The functions that write, review and sign off Proud Tek articles
summary: This page names the functions that write, review and sign off editorial content on proudtek.com. Like our sister brand RFIDAK, we credit roles rather than individuals: an editorial team byline and an RF / production engineering reviewer byline, each with a stable anchor that article bylines and structured data link to. Every technical article — anything citing a standard, a chip family or a regulatory requirement — is checked against the source named in its sources block before publication, and the corrections process on /about/corrections/ applies to all of it. Named individuals are not published until a verifiable public profile exists for them; until then a name would be an unverifiable claim, and we do not publish those.
heroPoints: Every editorial article on proudtek.com carries the Proud Tek Editorial Team byline and is reviewed by the RF / Production Engineering function.
Technical articles (anything citing a standard, a chip family or a regulatory requirement) are checked against the cited standard, datasheet or regulation before publication.
No named individuals are published without a verifiable public profile — the same disclosure model as rfidak.com, the RFID brand of the same company.
Conflicts of interest are handled by function: sales cannot direct editorial conclusions, and vendor relationships are disclosed on /about/disclosures/.

sections.title: Editorial team byline
sections.intro: Every article is published under the institutional byline below. Content is drafted by the function closest to the topic — sales engineering for buying guides, RF / production engineering for specification and compatibility pages, quality control for test and compliance content — and cross-checked against the cited source before it goes live.

features.title: Proud Tek Editorial Team
features.text: Institutional byline for Proud Tek's RFID and NFC buyer guides, comparisons and product pages. Drafted by the company's sales-engineering, RF / production engineering and quality-control functions; every technical claim is checked against the standard, chip-vendor datasheet or regulation cited in the article's sources block. The team also runs the corrections process described on /about/corrections/.

sections.title: Technical reviewer byline
sections.intro: Reviewers co-sign any article that cites a standard (ISO/IEC, GS1, EPCglobal, NFC Forum, ETSI, FCC, EU DPP) or that makes a performance or durability claim. The reviewer is a function, not a person: the engineering group that writes the specification the partner lines execute and signs off the batches with Quality Control.

features.title: Proud Tek RF / Production Engineering
features.text: Matches chip families and antenna designs to the buyer's installed readers or locks before production starts, writes the encoding specification, approves the first article and — with Quality Control — signs off every batch before release. On this site it is the reviewer of record for product specification pages, compatibility guides and technical articles; specification claims are checked against the vendor datasheet cited in each page's sources block.

callout.label: Why functions, not names
callout.text: A byline that names a role is one a buyer can hold us to: the function exists, is accountable for the order, and does not change when a person changes jobs. A byline that names a person is only worth publishing when the person's identity and credential can be verified from a public record — we hold that bar rather than publish names that cannot be checked.

sections.title: How a technical article is checked
sections.intro: The review is the same whichever function drafts the piece.

items.label: 1 — Draft with sources
items.text: The drafting function writes against the primary source: the standard text, the chip vendor's datasheet, the regulation or the GS1 specification. Every factual claim gets an entry in the article's sources block.

items.label: 2 — Engineering review
items.text: RF / Production Engineering checks chip, frequency, memory, encoding and compatibility statements against the cited datasheet and against what the partner lines actually produce; anything the function cannot verify is removed or labelled as an estimate.

items.label: 3 — Commercial and compliance review
items.text: MOQ, lead-time, sample-policy and certificate statements are checked against the published terms and the certificate registry on /about/certifications/ so no page promises what the company does not hold.

items.label: 4 — Publish and log
items.text: publishedAt / modifiedAt are set from the actual dates; any later factual change is logged on /about/corrections/.

sections.title: Adding a named contributor
sections.intro: We will publish a person's byline only when it can be verified. The bar is deliberately high.
bullets: Identity confirmed against at least one public professional profile (company registry filing, standards-body roster, patent register, conference programme or a professional network profile).
At least one verifiable credential checked against the issuing authority; unverifiable credentials are dropped, not labelled.
A signed disclosure of equity and paid relationships with any vendor the person might review, published with the entry.
A stable anchor on this page and a registry record with `type: Person` and the public profile in `sameAs`, so structured data and the visible byline stay consistent.

faq.question: Why don't your articles name the people who wrote them?
faq.answer: Because we cannot yet publish identities and credentials that a reader can verify from a public record, and a name without that is just a claim. Until we can, bylines credit the functions that actually produce and check the content — the same model rfidak.com, the RFID brand of the same company, uses. The functions are accountable for the content and for every order it leads to.

faq.question: Who reviews technical claims before publication?
faq.answer: The RF / Production Engineering function — the group that writes the encoding and antenna specifications the partner lines execute and that signs off production batches with Quality Control. It checks chip, frequency, memory, encoding and compatibility statements against the cited vendor datasheet or standard.

faq.question: Can I challenge something an article says?
faq.answer: Yes. Send the URL and the specific claim to editors@proudtek.com. We acknowledge within 2 business days and either correct the article and log the change on /about/corrections/ or explain, with the source, why the text stands.

faq.question: Will named authors return?
faq.answer: When a contributor's identity and at least one credential can be verified from a public record and the disclosure form is signed, yes — the entry will carry the profile link so readers can check it. We would rather publish an accurate institutional byline than an impressive unverifiable one.
